q: What is Figure A that is a type of waterproofing system made from natural clay material that swells when in contact with water to create a self-sealing barrier, commonly used below-grade?
n: Bentonite waterproofing uses sodium bentonite clay (in panels or mats) that swells when wet to form a self-sealing barrier against below-grade walls and slabs. Source: ACI 515.2R / manufacturer literature (CETCO Voltex).

q: What is Figure B that is a pre-formed membrane system consisting of bituminous sheets that are torch-applied or self-adhesive, providing a durable waterproof barrier for roofs and foundations?
n: Sheet bituminous waterproofing uses modified bitumen membranes that are torch-applied or self-adhesive, giving a durable barrier for roofs, decks and foundations. Source: ASTM D6164/D6222 (modified bitumen sheets); NRCA Roofing Manual.

q: What is Figure C that is a waterproofing method using a fluid-applied membrane brushed, rolled, or sprayed onto surfaces, curing to form a seamless protective layer?
n: Liquid-applied waterproofing (polyurethane, acrylic or bitumen-based) is brushed, rolled or sprayed on and cures into a seamless membrane. Source: ASTM C836 (liquid-applied membranes); manufacturer literature.

q: What is Figure D that is a flexible strip embedded in concrete joints to block water infiltration, typically used in water tanks, retaining walls, and basements?
n: A waterstop is a PVC, rubber or swelling strip cast across construction joints in tanks, basements and retaining walls, blocking water from passing through the joint. Source: ACI 350 (environmental concrete structures); ACI 224.3R.

q: What is Figure E that is a rigid or semi-flexible coating made from cement-based products with special additives, used to protect concrete from moisture and seepage?
n: Cementitious waterproofing is a cement-based coating with polymer or chemical additives, brushed or troweled on concrete to stop moisture and seepage. Source: ACI 515.2R; manufacturer literature (Sika, Thoro).

q: Which waterproofing is added directly into the concrete mix?
n: Integral waterproofing is an admixture added to the concrete mix at batching that reduces permeability throughout the concrete. Source: ACI 212.3R (chemical admixtures, permeability-reducing).

q: What keeps soil out of perforated basement drain pipes?
o: Packing gravel chips around the pipe
n: A geotextile filter fabric wrapped around a perforated drain (and its gravel bed) lets water in while keeping soil fines out, so the drain does not clog. Source: ASTM D4491 (geotextile permittivity); FHWA Geosynthetic Design Manual.

q: Which company is the major seller and distributor of Thoroseal and Sureseal waterproofing products?
n: Jardine Distribution is a major Philippine seller and distributor of the Thoroseal and Sureseal cementitious waterproofing lines. Source: Philippine distributor product listings.

q: Which insulation should be avoided for users allergic to newspaper dust, since it is made of recycled paper?
n: Cellulose insulation is made of recycled newsprint and cardboard, so it can release paper dust. People allergic to it should avoid it. Source: US DOE Energy Saver, Insulation Materials; ASTM C739 (cellulose insulation).

q: Which of the following is not an elastomeric waterproofing brand?
n: Thoroseal is a cementitious (cement-based) waterproof coating, not an elastomeric. The other brands are elastomeric (rubbery) coatings. Source: Thoro/Master Builders Solutions product data.

q: Which waterproofing best suits structures over water and highly corrosive settings?
n: Integral waterproofing protects the whole concrete mass rather than a surface layer that can be abraded or corroded away, so it suits marine structures and highly corrosive settings. Source: ACI 212.3R; ACI 357 (marine concrete).

q: Which insulation is called most eco-friendly because it is made of recycled paper, and is treated to resist fire?
n: Cellulose insulation is mostly recycled paper treated with borates for fire and pest resistance, making it one of the most eco-friendly insulations. Source: US DOE Energy Saver, Insulation Materials; ASTM C739.

q: Which Filipino company makes Mighty Bond and Elastoseal?
n: Mighty Bond (instant glue) and Elastoseal (elastomeric sealant and waterproofing) are products of Pioneer Adhesives Inc., a Filipino company. Source: Pioneer Adhesives company website.

q: What affordable membrane is laid under a slab on grade to stop moisture rising by capillary action?
n: A polyethylene sheet (about 0.15–0.25 mm, 6–10 mil) laid under a slab on grade is the cheap, standard barrier against rising ground moisture and capillary wicking. Source: ACI 302.1R (vapor retarders); ASTM E1745.

q: Xypex is a brand of ______ waterproofing.
n: Xypex is a crystalline waterproofing: its chemicals react with moisture and cement by-products to grow insoluble crystals that block the capillary pores of concrete. Source: Xypex Chemical Corporation product literature.

q: What is used to stop or reduce moisture penetration through concrete?
n: A damp proofer is a coating or treatment that stops or reduces moisture penetrating through concrete or masonry (not water under pressure). Source: ACI 515.2R; ASTM D1227 (dampproofing).

q: What is the entry or slow passage of water into a structure called?
n: Seepage is the slow entry or passage of water into or through a structure's material and joints, as distinct from an open leak. Source: ACI Concrete Terminology (CT); construction dictionaries.

q: What is the general term for a sheet placed in a structure to limit moisture entry?
n: A moisture barrier is the general term for a sheet or layer placed in an assembly to limit the entry of water and moisture. Source: ASTM E1745; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What layer reduces the flow of water vapor into a roof system?
n: A vapor barrier (vapor retarder) is a low-permeance layer that limits water vapor diffusing into the roof or wall assembly, where it could condense. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (moisture control); ASTM E1745.

q: A polyethylene sheet used to block water vapor is a:
n: Polyethylene film is the most common vapor barrier, blocking water vapor in slabs, walls and roofs. Source: ASTM E1745; ACI 302.1R.

q: Which waterproofing is made of capillary-active chemicals with quartz sand and cement?
n: Crystalline products are mixes of portland cement, fine quartz sand and active (capillary) chemicals that react to plug concrete pores. Source: ACI 212.3R (crystalline admixtures); Xypex product literature.

q: What type of waterproofing is most appropriate for a firewall?
n: A firewall faces sun, rain and building movement. A flexible elastomeric coating bridges hairline cracks and keeps rain out of the masonry. Source: Paint and coating manufacturer data (Boysen, Davies); ASTM D6904.

q: Which waterproofing swells on contact with water and is used below grade?
n: Bentonite (sodium montmorillonite clay) swells many times its volume on contact with water and self-seals. It is used against below-grade walls and slabs. Source: CETCO bentonite product literature; ACI 515.2R.

q: Which waterproofing is commonly applied under tiles, with Plexibond as a popular example?
n: Polymer-modified cementitious coatings (such as Plexibond) are commonly brushed on toilet floors and walls before tiling to make the substrate waterproof. Source: Manufacturer product literature; ANSI A118.10 (waterproof membranes for tile).

q: To avoid leaks on a concrete roof deck, what should be done?
o: Provide proper slope toward the floor drain
Use membrane waterproofing and admixture in the concrete
Apply elastomeric paint after concrete pouring
Add waterproofing admixture to concrete before pouring
n: A concrete roof deck should be protected twice: a waterproofing admixture reduces the concrete's permeability, and a membrane on top seals cracks and joints the concrete alone cannot. Source: ACI 515.2R (protective barrier systems); ACI 212.3R (permeability-reducing admixtures).

q: How far should balcony waterproofing extend?
o: The whole floor and partly up the adjacent walls
The whole floor and full height of the walls
n: Balcony waterproofing covers the whole floor and turns up the adjoining walls (about 150–300 mm) as an upstand, so water cannot get in at the wall–floor joint. Source: ANSI A108/A118.10 (tile waterproofing); NRCA Roofing Manual (base flashings).

q: What is the main job of flashing in a building envelope?
o: Directing water away from joints and seams
n: Flashing is sheet metal or membrane placed at joints and junctions (roof–wall, openings, penetrations) to direct water away and out of the building envelope. Source: SMACNA Architectural Sheet Metal Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.
